targets.Description: The website relates to St George’s Hospital, formerly Stafford County Asylum, which was one of the earliest in the country opening in 1818. The early buildings were abandoned some years ago and allowed to fall into disrepair, and be the target of vandalism, which has been a major local concern because the site is fairly central in the town. In the grounds there is now new housing built, and the hospital buildings that can be saved are also now under development, so there is renewed local interest, and the grounds are now open for people to get a much closer look after years of being boarded up. The website also covers the private asylum called Coton Hill which opened in the 1850s and remained open until the site was used to build the new district hospital in the 1970s, and only the chapel and lodge buildings remain of the original buildings. The website incorporates information from other former members of staff of the Staffordshire Record Office, and reminiscences, photographs etc.
